---
title: "Stage 1 – Credibility and the three Rs"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at Part 1](../../slides/housing-one-day-methods.html#/part-1-credibility-and-tools){target="_blank"} in its own tab, where the `s` key opens the speaker view with the notes of each slide, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The route opens on the question that gives the course its name. Reproduction, robustness and replication are three different ways of repeating a study, and the three can return different verdicts on the same paper, as the four cases of the course show. This stage takes the talk from Part 1 of the deck of the housing-audit case, the first case of the route, and installs the tools, so that a machine that will not cooperate is found now rather than in the middle of a task. It takes about five and a quarter hours.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, Part 1 | What social science is for; false positives and forking paths; the evidence from replications and many-analysts studies; incentives and questionable research practices; the red-card study, in which twenty-nine teams analysed one dataset; why 'replication' names three different operations; the practices of open research; the SCORE programme and its three studies, with the finding that their results do not travel together; Multi100 from the position of an analyst inside it; and the computational toolchain. Read each slide with its speaker notes. | 90 minutes |
| [Setup](../../setup.qmd) | Install R, Quarto and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the workspace of the housing-audit case and run `source("R/check_setup.R")` until every line prints OK; the last check fits the reference specification and prints −19.97 percentage points. This is Task 1 of the first case. Open the [browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-1-setup) of the case once as well, which runs every task in a browser tab if your installation fails, and keep the [help page](../../help.qmd) at hand for the problems that others have met. | 60 minutes, once |
| [The opening page](../../index.qmd#cases), the four cases and [the five tasks](../../index.qmd#exercise) | Read the four case cards in the order of the route, opening each card for what the case teaches, its data, and what reproduction, robustness and replication found on it. Then read the five tasks that every case repeats. | 20 minutes |
| [Resources – Glossary](../../resources.qmd#glossary) | Reproducibility, robustness and replicability defined side by side, with the other terms that the slides used. | 25 minutes |
| [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd) | [What an IDE does](../../companion/ide.qmd#sec-what) and the section on the IDE that you chose, then [the six steps](../../companion/ide.qmd#sec-try) at the end of the module, in the workspace that you have just installed; they use every pane that the tasks need. | 60 minutes |
| [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd), from [R and the IDE](../../companion/intro-r.qmd#sec-what) to [Packages](../../companion/intro-r.qmd#sec-packages) | The console, the script and the report; objects and vectors, and why the mean of a column of 0s and 1s is a share; data frames; installing and loading packages. | 60 minutes |

**Shortcuts.** If R, Quarto and an IDE are already on your machine, download the workspace, run the check and install what it reports as missing, which takes about a quarter of an hour. If you already work in one of the three IDEs, take only the six steps of the IDE module. If you write R, leave the R module until stage 2, which says what to read in it.

**By the end of the stage** you have R, Quarto and an IDE installed, the workspace of the housing-audit case passing its setup check, and a paragraph in your own words that tells reproduction, robustness and replication apart and says what each of them found on one of the four cases.
